en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from al-Shaybani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, who said: I asked A'ishah about incantations, and she said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) granted a concession to a household among the Ansar to recite incantations against every venomous creature.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me; (Second chain) and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us; (Third chain) and Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to me: Rawh narrated to us; (Fourth chain) and Uqbah ibn Mukram and Ahmad ibn Uthman al-Nawfali narrated to us—they said: Abu Asim narrated to us; both of them from Ibn Jurayj: Ziyad informed me; all of them from Ibn Shihab, with the chain of transmission of Malik, similar to his hadith. And none of them had in their hadith "hoping for its blessing" except in the hadith of Malik. And in the hadith of Yunus and Ziyad: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), whenever he had an ailment, would blow lightly over himself with the protective surahs and wipe over himself with his hand.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from A'ishah: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), whenever he suffered an ailment, would recite over himself the protective surahs and blow lightly. Then when his pain became severe, I used to recite over him and wipe him with his own hand, hoping for its blessing.

Surayj ibn Yunus and Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to me—they said: Abbad ibn Abbad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from A'ishah, who said: Whenever anyone of his family became sick, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would blow lightly over them reciting the protective surahs. Then, when he fell ill with the illness from which he died, I began to blow lightly over him and wipe him with his own hand, because it was of greater blessing than my hand. And in the narration of Yahya ibn Ayyub: "with protective verses."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Isa ibn Yunus informed us; both of them from Hisham, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is that of Abu Kurayb—they said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to treat with this incantation: "Remove the harm, O Lord of mankind; in Your Hand is healing; none can remove it except You."

Al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya narrated to me: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Mansur, from Ibrahim and Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to... similar to the hadith of Abu Awanah and Jarir.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to us—they said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) visited a sick person to supplicate for him, he would say: "Remove the harm, O Lord of mankind, and heal; You are the Healer, there is no healing except Your healing—a healing that leaves behind no illness." And in the narration of Abu Bakr: "he supplicated for him and said: 'and You are the Healer.'"

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Masruq, from A'ishah: that whenever the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) visited a sick person, he would say: "Remove the harm, O Lord of mankind; heal him, You are the Healer; there is no healing except Your healing—a healing that leaves behind no illness."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us; (Second chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (Third chain) and Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; (Fourth chain) and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us; both of them from Shu'bah; (Fifth chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Bakr ibn Khallad narrated to us—they said: Yahya—and he is al-Qattan—narrated to us, from Sufyan; all of them from al-A'mash, with the chain of transmission of Jarir. In the hadith of Hushaym and Shu'bah: "he wiped him with his hand." He said: And in the hadith of al-Thawri: "he wiped him with his right hand." And he said at the conclusion of the hadith of Yahya from Sufyan from al-A'mash: He said: So I narrated it to Mansur, and he narrated to me from Ibrahim, from Masruq, from A'ishah, similar to it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: informed us, and Zuhayr said—and the wording is his: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: Whenever anyone among us suffered an ailment, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would wipe him with his right hand and then say: "Remove the harm, O Lord of mankind, and heal; You are the Healer, there is no healing except Your healing—a healing that leaves behind no illness." When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) fell ill and became heavy with sickness, I took his hand to do to him what he used to do, but he pulled his hand away from my hand and then said: "O Allah, forgive me and join me with the Exalted Companion." She said: So I went to look, and behold, he had passed away.

Harun ibn Abdillah narrated to us: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Hisham ibn Zayd saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrating that a Jewish woman put poison in some meat, then brought it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... similar to the hadith of Khalid.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Zayd, from Anas: that a Jewish woman brought the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) a poisoned sheep, and he ate from it. She was brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he questioned her about that. She said: "I intended to kill you." He said: "Allah would never give you power over that"—or he said: "over me." He said: They asked: "Shall we not kill her?" He said: "No." He said: And I continued to perceive the effect of it in the palate of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from A'ishah, who said: Magic was worked on the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and Abu Kurayb cited the hadith with its story similar to the hadith of Ibn Numayr, and said in it: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went to the well and looked at it, and by it were date palms. And she said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, bring it out!" And he did not say: "Will you not burn it?" nor did he mention: "so I ordered it and it was buried."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from A'ishah, who said: A Jew from the Jews of Banu Zurayq named Labid ibn al-A'sam worked magic on the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), to the extent that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was made to imagine that he had done something when he had not done it. Until one day—or one night—the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) supplicated, then supplicated, then supplicated, and then said: "O A'ishah, do you know that Allah has answered me regarding that which I inquired of Him? Two men came to me; one of them sat at my head and the other at my feet. The one at my head said to the one at my feet—or the one at my feet said to the one at my head: 'What is the man's ailment?' He said: 'He is bewitched.' He asked: 'Who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labid ibn al-A'sam.' He asked: 'In what?' He said: 'In a comb and the hairs falling from it, and the spadix of a male date palm.' He asked: 'Where is it?' He said: 'In the well of Dhu Arwan.'" She said: So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went to it with some of his companions, then said: "O A'ishah, by Allah, its water was like the infusion of henna, and its date palms were like the heads of devils." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, did you not burn it?" He said: "No. As for me, Allah has healed me, and I disliked to stir up evil against the people." So he ordered it and it was buried.

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir, and Ahmad ibn Khirash narrated to us—Abdullah said: informed us, and the other two said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The evil eye is a reality; and if anything could precede the divine decree, the evil eye would precede it. And when you are asked to perform washing, then wash."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which was: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The evil eye is a reality."

Bishr ibn Hilal al-Sawwaf narrated to us: Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id: that Gabriel came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Muhammad, are you suffering from an ailment?" He said: "Yes." Gabriel said: "In the Name of Allah I recite over you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye; may Allah heal you; in the Name of Allah I recite over you."

Muhammad ibn Abi Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz al-Darawardi narrated to us, from Yazid—and he is Ibn Abdillah ibn Usamah ibn al-Had—from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that she said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was ill, Gabriel would recite over him, saying: "In the Name of Allah He clears you, and from every disease He heals you, and from the evil of an envier when he envies, and the evil of everyone possessing an evil eye."
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Isa ibn Yunus informed us; (Second chain) and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us; both of them from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Numayr, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is that of Yahya; Yahya said: informed us, and the others said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When there are three of you, let not two converse in private to the exclusion of their companion, for that will grieve him."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us—they said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Mansur; (Second chain) and Zuhayr ibn Harb, Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is that of Zuhayr; Ishaq said: informed us, and the other two said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When there are three of you, let not two converse in private to the exclusion of the other until you mingle with other people, lest that should grieve him."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr and Ibn Numayr narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us; (Third chain) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us—they said: Yahya—and he is Ibn Sa'id—narrated to us; all of them from Ubaydullah; (Fourth chain) and Qutaybah and Ibn Rumh narrated to us, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd; (Fifth chain) and Abu al-Rabi' and Abu Kamil narrated to us—they said: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub; (Sixth chain) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Ayyub ibn Musa; all of them from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), in the sense of the hadith of Malik.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When there are three, let not two converse in private to the exclusion of the third."

Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Ghubari narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah: that Asma' said: "I used to do household work for al-Zubayr, and he had a horse that I used to tend. No chore was harder upon me than tending the horse: I used to cut grass for it, look after it, and groom it." He said: "Then she obtained a servant: captives were brought to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he gave her a servant." She said: "She relieved me of tending the horse and lifted its burden from me. Then a man came to me and said: 'O Umm Abdillah, I am a poor man, and I wish to sell goods in the shade of your house.' She said: 'If I permit you, al-Zubayr will refuse; so come and ask me while al-Zubayr is present.' So he came and said: 'O Umm Abdillah, I am a poor man, and I wish to sell goods in the shade of your house.' She said: 'Have you nowhere in Medina except my house?' Al-Zubayr said to her: 'What is wrong with you that you should forbid a poor man from selling?' So he used to sell until he earned a livelihood, and then I sold him the servant girl. Al-Zubayr entered upon me while her price was in my lap, and said: 'Gift it to me.' She said: 'I have already given it away in charity.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Ala' Abu Kurayb al-Hamdani narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham: my father informed me, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: Al-Zubayr married me, and he possessed neither wealth nor slave nor anything on earth except his horse. She said: I used to feed his horse, provide for its maintenance, and groom it. I would crush date stones for his water-carrying camel, feed it, fetch water, stitch his leather bucket, and knead dough, though I was not good at baking bread; so some neighbor women of the Ansar used to bake for me, and they were honorable women. She said: And I used to carry date stones on my head from the land of al-Zubayr which the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had granted him, and it was at a distance of two-thirds of a farsakh. She said: One day I came while carrying date stones on my head, and I met the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) who was with a group of his companions. He called me and then made his camel kneel so that he might carry me behind him. She said: But I felt shy and I knew your sense of jealousy. Thereupon al-Zubayr said: "By Allah, your carrying date stones on your head was harder upon me than your riding with him!" She said: Until Abu Bakr later sent me a servant, who relieved me of tending the horse, so it was as if he had set me free.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from A'ishah, who said: An effeminate man used to enter upon the wives of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and they counted him among those men who have no sexual desire. She said: One day the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered while he was with one of his wives, describing a woman and saying: "When she comes forward, she approaches with four, and when she turns back, she turns away with eight." The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, I see this person understands what is here! He must never enter upon you." She said: So they secluded themselves from him.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—they said: Waki' narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us; (Third chain) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; all of them from Hisham; (Fourth chain) and Abu Kurayb also narrated to us—and the wording is this: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah: that an effeminate man was with her while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was in the house, and he said to the brother of Umm Salamah: "O Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, if Allah grants you victory over al-Ta'if tomorrow, I will guide you to the daughter of Ghaylan, for she approaches with four and turns back with eight." He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) heard him and said: "These people should never enter upon you."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abu Awanah informed us; and Qutaybah also said: Abd al-Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us; both from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you stands up..." and in the hadith of Abu Awanah: "Whoever stands up from his seat and then returns to it, he has the greatest right to it."

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil—and he is Ibn Ubaydillah—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "None of you should make his brother stand on Friday and then take his place to sit in it; but rather he should say: 'Make room.'"
